cases.sentence: ___ Вронского с расчесанными бакенбардами, похожий на камер Юнкера, входил тоже.
cases.translation: Vronsky's footman, with combed side-whiskers, resembling a gentleman of the bedchamber, was also entering.
cases.explain: Лакей is the subject of the verb входил (was entering), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: К этому ее отказу относились намеки ___ княгини Тверской.
cases.translation: This refusal of hers was hinted at by the note from Princess Tverskaya.
cases.explain: Записки depends on the noun намеки (hints of the note), a noun-plus-noun construction that requires the genitive case.

cases.sentence: «А вы бы пошли», — обратилась она к ___, «с Машей попробовали бы крокет-гроунд там, где подстригли».
cases.translation: "You should go," she turned to Tushkevich, "and try the croquet ground with Masha, where they've mowed it."
cases.explain: The preposition к (to/toward) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Подвинув ___ к Анне, она достала пахитоску и, вложив серебряную ручку, закурила ее.
cases.translation: Having pushed the cup toward Anna, she took out a cigarette holder and, fitting the silver mouthpiece, lit it.
cases.explain: Чашку is the direct object of подвинув (having moved), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Ни минуты не думая, Анна села с ___ Бетси к столу и, не читая, приписала внизу.
cases.translation: Without a moment's thought, Anna sat down at the table with Betsy's letter and, without reading it, added a line at the bottom.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case here.

cases.translation: They were in the small study.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) governs the prepositional case here, expressing location.

cases.sentence: У меня одна дама к обеду остается без ___.
cases.translation: I have one lady left for dinner without a man.
cases.explain: The preposition без (without) governs the genitive case.

reading.ru: Общество партии Кракета, на которое княгиня Тверская приглашала Анну, должно было состоять из двух дам с их поклонниками.
reading.question: What was the croquet party Anna was invited to supposed to consist of?
reading.correct: Two ladies and their admirers
reading.explain: The text states the party was to consist of two ladies and their admirers.

reading.ru: Кроме того, старый Стремов, один из влиятельных людей Петербурга, поклонник Лизы Меркаловой, был по службе враг Алексея Александровича.
reading.question: What was Stremov's relationship to Karenin?
options: A professional enemy through their official duties
reading.correct: A professional enemy through their official duties
reading.explain: The text says Stremov was Karenin's enemy through their service duties.

reading.ru: Теперь же Анна, в надежде увидать Вронского, пожелала ехать.
reading.question: Why did Anna change her mind and decide to go after all?
options: She hoped to see Vronsky there
Her husband ordered her to go
Betsy threatened to end their friendship
She wanted to meet Liza Merkalova
reading.correct: She hoped to see Vronsky there
reading.explain: The text says Anna now wished to go in hope of seeing Vronsky.

reading.ru: В то время, как она входила, лакей Вронского с расчесанными бакенбардами, похожий на камер Юнкера, входил тоже.
reading.question: Who entered at the same time as Anna?
reading.correct: Vronsky's footman
reading.explain: As Anna entered, Vronsky's footman, with combed side-whiskers, was entering too.

reading.ru: Анна узнала его и тут только вспомнила, что Вронский вчера сказал, что не приедет.
reading.question: What did Anna suddenly remember on recognizing the footman?
options: That Vronsky had said yesterday he would not come
That she had forgotten her invitation
That the footman owed her money
reading.correct: That Vronsky had said yesterday he would not come
reading.explain: Recognizing the footman, Anna remembered that Vronsky had told her the day before that he would not come.

reading.ru: Ей хотелось вернуться назад и послать ему письмо, чтобы он приехал к ней или самой ехать к нему.
reading.question: What impulse did Anna feel on hearing Vronsky's note had arrived?
options: To turn back and send him a letter, or go to him herself
To leave the party immediately without a word
To ask Betsy to cancel the party
reading.correct: To turn back and send him a letter, or go to him herself
reading.explain: She wanted to go back and send him a letter asking him to come to her, or to go to him herself.

reading.ru: Но она была в туалете, который, она знала, шел к ней.
reading.question: What comforted Anna despite her indecision?
options: She knew her dress suited her well
She had already spoken with Vronsky
She had received a reassuring letter
Betsy had promised to help her
reading.correct: She knew her dress suited her well
reading.explain: The text notes that she was wearing a toilette she knew became her.

reading.ru: Встретив шедшую к ней Бетси в белом, поразившем ее свою элегантностью туалете, Анна улыбнулась ей, как всегда.
reading.question: How did Anna react on meeting Betsy?
options: She smiled at her as always
She scolded her for being late
reading.correct: She smiled at her as always
reading.explain: Meeting Betsy, who came toward her in a striking white dress, Anna smiled at her as usual.

reading.ru: «Я устала и только что хотела выпить чашку чая, пока они приедут».
reading.question: What did Betsy say she wanted to do while waiting for the other guests?
reading.correct: Drink a cup of tea
reading.explain: Betsy says she is tired and wanted to drink a cup of tea while waiting for the others to arrive.

reading.ru: Тем более, что я не могу пробыть у вас долго, мне необходимо к старой вреде.
reading.question: What excuse did Anna give for not being able to stay long?
options: She needed to visit old Madame Vrede
She had to return home to her son
reading.correct: She needed to visit old Madame Vrede
reading.explain: Anna says she cannot stay long because she must go see old Madame Vrede.

reading.ru: «Нет, я вас не пущу ни за что», — отвечала Бетси, внимательно вглядываясь в лицо Анны.
reading.question: How did Betsy respond to Anna's plan to leave early?
options: She refused to let her go, watching her face closely
She asked Anna to take her along
reading.correct: She refused to let her go, watching her face closely
reading.explain: Betsy answers that she will not let Anna go for anything, studying her face intently.

reading.ru: «Алексей сделал нам ложный прыжок», — сказала она по-французски.
reading.question: What did Betsy say in French after reading Vronsky's note?
options: That Alexei had let them down
That Alexei was on his way
reading.correct: That Alexei had let them down
reading.explain: Betsy reads the note and remarks in French that Alexei had made them a false jump, meaning he had let them down.

reading.ru: Анна знала, что Бетси все знает.
reading.question: What did Anna believe about Betsy's awareness of her affair?
options: That Betsy had guessed only part of it
That Betsy did not care either way
reading.correct: That Betsy knew everything
reading.explain: The text states plainly that Anna knew Betsy knew everything about her situation with Vronsky.

reading.ru: Однако надо написать Алексею, и Бетси села за стол, написала несколько строк, вложила в конверт.
reading.question: What did Betsy do to help arrange things?
options: She wrote a note to Alexei and put it in an envelope
She sent her footman to fetch Vronsky
She asked Tushkevich to write the note
reading.correct: She wrote a note to Alexei and put it in an envelope
reading.explain: Betsy sat at the table, wrote a few lines to Alexei, and put them in an envelope.

reading.ru: Ни минуты не думая, Анна села с письмом Бетси к столу и, не читая, приписала внизу.
reading.question: What did Anna do with Betsy's letter?
options: She added a line of her own at the bottom without hesitation
She read it aloud to Betsy
reading.correct: She added a line of her own at the bottom without hesitation
reading.explain: Without a moment's thought, Anna sat down with Betsy's letter and, without reading it, added a line at the bottom.

reading.ru: «Мне необходимо вас видеть. Приезжайте к саду в Реде. Я буду там в шесть часов».
reading.question: What did Anna's added message to Vronsky say?
options: That she needed to see him and would be at the Vrede garden at six
That he should not come at all
That she wanted to meet him the next morning
reading.correct: That she needed to see him and would be at the Vrede garden at six
reading.explain: Anna writes that she must see him, asks him to come to the garden at Vrede's, and says she will be there at six.

reading.ru: Действительно, за чаем, который им принесли на столике под носе в прохладную маленькую гостиную, между двумя женщинами завязался экозий чат, какой и обещала княгиня Тверская до приезда гостей.
reading.question: What began between Anna and Betsy over tea?
options: A cozy chat, as Princess Tverskaya had promised
reading.correct: A cozy chat, as Princess Tverskaya had promised
reading.explain: Over tea in the small drawing room, the two women began the cozy chat that Princess Tverskaya had promised before the guests arrived.

reading.ru: Скажите, пожалуйста, что такое ее отношение к князю Калужскому, так называемому Мишке?
reading.question: What did Anna ask Betsy about Liza Merkalova?
options: What Liza's relationship with Prince Kaluzhsky, called Mishka, really was
reading.correct: What Liza's relationship with Prince Kaluzhsky, called Mishka, really was
reading.explain: Anna asks Betsy what Liza's relationship to Prince Kaluzhsky, nicknamed Mishka, actually is.

reading.ru: Муж Лизы Меркаловой носит за ней пледы и всегда готов к услугам.
reading.question: What role does Liza Merkalova's husband play, according to Betsy?
options: He carries her rugs and is always ready to serve her
He forbids her from going into society
He accompanies her to every ball
reading.correct: He carries her rugs and is always ready to serve her
reading.explain: Betsy explains that Liza's husband simply carries her plaids and is always at her service.

reading.ru: «Вы будете на празднике Роландаки?» — спросила Анна, чтобы переменить разговор.
reading.question: Why did Anna ask Betsy about the Rolandaki party?
options: To change the subject of conversation
Because Betsy had asked her first
reading.correct: To change the subject of conversation
reading.explain: The text explicitly says Anna asked about the Rolandaki party in order to change the conversation.

reading.ru: Лиза — это одна из тех наивных натур, которые, как дети, не понимают, что хорошо и что дурно.
reading.question: How does Betsy describe Liza Merkalova's nature?
options: As a naive nature, like a child who doesn't distinguish good from bad
reading.correct: As a naive nature, like a child who doesn't distinguish good from bad
reading.explain: Betsy calls Liza one of those naive natures who, like children, do not understand what is good and what is bad.

reading.ru: «Ужасный ребенок, ужасный ребенок», повторила Бетси.
reading.question: What phrase does Betsy repeat about Anna at the end of their conversation?
reading.correct: "Terrible child, terrible child"
reading.explain: Betsy repeats the phrase "ужасный ребенок" (terrible child) about Anna at the close of the scene.
